full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J.: On an application under section 561A CrPC made by informant petitioner Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy, a Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong and the opposite party Nos. 2-5 to show cause why the judgment and order dated 26.4.93 passed by the Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Misc. Case No. 431 of 1992 arising out of the orders dated 30.6.92 and 1.7.92 of the Thana Magistrate, Lohagara in GR Case No. 63 of 1992 arising out of Lohagara Police Station Case No. 12 (6)/92 dated 23.6.92 under section 366 of the Penal Code should not be quashed and why the victim girl namely, Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua, daughter of Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy (village doctor) now in the Chittagong Jail custody should not be handed over to the custody of the petitioner (father) as her lawful guardian, or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The aforesaid First Information Report was recorded as Lohagara Police Station Case No. 12 dated 23.6.92 under section 366 of the Penal Code. The alleged victim daughter Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua was recovered by the Police from the custody of the accuseds and produced before the court of Thana Magistrate Lohagara on 30.6.92. The Sub-Inspector of police Lohagara submitted an application to the Thana Magistrate, seeking 10 days' police remand of Munni Roy for medical examination to ascertain the victim's age and whether she had been raped. The informant father filed an application praying for 'Jimma' of his daughter Munni Roy. The Thana Magistrate in GR Case No. 63 of 1992 by an order on 30.6.92 directed the file to be put up and fixed the following day i.e. 1.7.92 for recording the statement of victim Munni Roy. It appears from the lower court record that on 1.7.92 victim Munni Roy made a statement before the Thana Magistrate Lohagara, district Chittagong and she signed her statement as Ayesha Siddiqua (Munni). She stated that her name was Ayesha Siddiqua Munni and that at present she had no father. Her house was at village Padua, PS Lohagara, and her age was 19 years. She was reading in class IX. She became a Muslim by reciting the kalema and that nobody forced her to embrace Islam Thereafter she met accused Saiful Islam and married him of her own free will. She went to the office of the Muslim Marriage Registrar and Kazi on her own accord with her husband Saiful Islam and that her elder brother Joy Prakash Roy alias Serajul Islam was with her at that time. Her said brother was also a Muslim. Her brother was a witness to the marriage as well as to the registered Nikanama. She was living with her husband and she wanted to stay with her husband (accused Saiful Islam). She said that she would not go with her father informant Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy. 

 4. It appears from the lower court record that the said Thana Magistrate also recorded the statement of Munni Roy's (alias Ayesha Siddiqua) brother. The brother made the statement and signed his name as Serajul Islam. He said that his name was Serajul Islam, that previously his name was Joy Prakash Roy, that his house was at village Padua, that he was aged 25 years and that he did not prosecute his study any more. He and his sister Munni Roy went together and embraced the religion of Islam voluntarily. He stated that nobody forced his sister Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua to marry and that he was a witness to the marriage of his sister to accused Saiful Islam. He stated that he was a Muslim and that he was staying at that time in the house of his foster father Rafiq Member at village Padua. 

 5. The order dated 1.7.92 passed by the Thana Magistrate Lohagara in GR Case No. 12 of 1992 which is Annexure 'C' to the petition shows that an application was filed by the police on 1.9.92 for adding the charge under section 366A Penal Code against the accused persons. On that day the victim's brother Serajul Islam alias Joy Prakash Roy had also applied for recording his statement which was recorded by the Magistrate as narrated above. It appears from the order that the Nikanama of the marriage of Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua to accused Md. Saiful Islam was also submitted. A photo copy of the said nikanama is found in the lower court record. The Thana Magistrate also stated in the said order that the victim had become a Muslim voluntarily on her own free will, that the victim girl was not forced and that she freely got married to a Muslim boy. He also noted from the statement made by the victim's brother Serajul Islam alias Joy Prakash Roy that he, Joy Prakash Roy became a Muslim voluntarily and that he was a witness to the victim's marriage to accused Saiful Islam. The said Serajul Islam stated his age to be 25 years. It is from these statements made by victim Ayesha Siddiqua alias Munni Roy and her brother Serajul Islam alias Joy Prakash Roy that the Thana Magistrate prima facie held that both of them became Muslim on their own free will and that the victim Ayesha Siddiqua got married to accused Saiful Islam. He further found that earlier another member of the family, a brother of Ayesha Siddiqua and Serajul Islam, had also embraced Islam. The question that stood before him related to the victim's age. The prosecution claimed that the victim was a minor and her age was stated to be 13 years in the First Information Report. But, according to the statement of the victim and the Nikanama, she was 19 years. It is also stated in the order sheet that both the prosecution and the State made submission to take the victim girl to judicial custody. After considering the facts and circumstances he held that since the victim girl had become a Muslim according to the legal rites, she should be allowed to stay with her foster father Rafiqul Islam and her husband accused Saiful Islam. By the same order the Thana Magistrate directed that whenever the victim girl was required for medical examination she should be allowed to go for such examination with the Investigating Officer. The informant petitioner being aggrieved by the said order dated 1.7.92 passed by the Thana Magistrate in GR Case No. 63 of 1992 preferred Criminal Motion No. 431 of 1992 on 4.7.92 before the court of Sessions Judge, Chittagong under sections 435/439A CrPC. The learned Sessions Judge called for record of GR Case No. 63 of 1992 and fixed the case for hearing on 18.7.92. The learned Sessions Judge by order dated 4.7.92 also directed the Thana Magistrate to arrange medical examination of the victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua for the determination of her age by the Principal, Chittagong Medical College Hospital by forming a Medical Board. The learned Sessions Judge also directed that the victim's father informant Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy (village Doctor) should be permitted to remain present before the Medical Board for identification of the victim girl. The relevant portion of the Sessions Judge's order dated 4.7.92, as we find in Annexure 'D' to the petition,reads as follows : 

 "Petitioner has filed a petition praying for directing OP 2 through the Officer in Charge & the learned Magistrate, Lohagara Police Station to produce the victim Munni Roy before the Court of Sessions on the grounds stated therein. Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, admit the application under sections 435/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Call for the LC record. Issue notice to the OPs fixing 18.7.92 for hearing. 

 6. As per order of the Sessions Judge, the Officer-in-Charge of Lohagara Police Station through Thana Magistrate, Lohagara submitted an application before the Principal, Chittagong Medical College Hospital on 13.7.92 for medical examination of the victim. The Principal, Chittagong Medical College Hospital vide Memo. No. 2383/3(1) dated 13.7.92 constituted a Medical Board comprising of one Chairman, Professor Hashin Ahmed and two members namely, Associate Professor Dr. Anwar Ara Begum and Assistant Professor Dr. Shamsunnahar in pursuance of the said letter fixing the time 10-00 AM on 16.6.92 for Medical examination and requesting the Officer-in-Charge Lohagara police station to bring the victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua before the office of the Professor, Radiologist Department, Chittagong Medical College Hospital on the said date and time. The said letter was dated 13.7.92. On 16.7.92 the constituted Medical Board in the presence of the Officer-in-Charge Lohagara Police Station, the Zimmadar of the victim girl namely Rafiqul Islam and the victim's father informant Bimal Kanti Roy, conducted medical examination of Munni Roy in part. The Principal, Chittagong Medical College Hospital by a notice under Memo. No. 2423 dated 19.7.92 fixed for rest of the medical examination within 22.7.92 and informed the same to the Officer-in-Charge through registered post. It appears from the lower court's record the victim Ayesha Siddiqua alias Munni Roy. by a Memo dated 23.6.92 to which her photograph is attached, had agreed to undergo the medical examination. The said Memo.contains the signature of the victim's father Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy who signed the memo as witness and identified with his address written in his own hand. The medical report of the Radiologist which was signed on 18.7.92 is found in the lower court record and reads as follows: 

 7. It appears from the Radiologist report that the medical examination of the victim Ayesha Siddiqua (Munni Roy) was held on 16.7.92 and she was again identified by her father Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy and the SI of Lohagara Police Station on the same date. It also appears that from the lower court's record that the rest of the medical examination of victim Ayesha Siddiqua was also held on 21.7.92 and signed by the said examining Doctors on 30.8.92. The medical report reads as follows: 

 It is alleged by the petitioner that the medical examination was to be held on 22.7.92 and accordingly, the Officer-in-Charge told the informant to remain present at the police station on that date to go before the Medical Board However, it is alleged that the Zimmadar of the victim did not appear at the police station along with the victim on 22.7.92 and so the Officer-in-Charge had to write a letter to the Principal, Chittagong Medical College for fixing another date for medical examination of the victim. But on the same date the Zimmadar of the victim appeared before the police station and verbally informed the Officer-in-Charge that the medical examination of the victim had been concluded on 21.7.92, and, the Zimmadar had shown a certificate given by two members of the Medical Board which was allegedly seized by the Officer-in-Charge and kept in the record. The certificate issued by the two doctors confirmed that the medical examination of victim Ayesha Siddiqua alias Munni Roy was completed on 21.7.92 at the Chittagong Medical College Forensic Medicine Division. The informant then on 25.7.92 filed an application before the Sessions Judge complaining of the irregularities and the violation of the court's order in respect of the medical examination, upon which the Sessions Judge on 25.7.92 directed the Officer-in-Charge, Lohagara Police Station to enquire into the allegation and to submit a report within 7 days. The Officer-in-Charge Lohagara Police Station on 28.7.92 submitted a report before the Judge which is annexed to the petition as Annexure 'J' to the petition and reads as follows: 

 11. Mr. Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the informant petitioner, has, inter alia, submitted that the learned Sessions Judge upon misconception of law, inter alia, held that the age of the victim girl was close to the vicinity of 16 years as indicated in the medical examination report, and, the said medical examination report was fabricated and created. It is also argued that Sessions Judge by his judgment illegally and arbitrarily released the victim girl from the judicial custody with liberty to go anywhere with whoever she liked wrongly accepting the age of the victim girl to be 16 years 7 months on 27.4.93 acted beyond his jurisdiction to determine the age of the victim girl on the basis of medical examination report which was spurious. He further submitted that there was miscarriage of justice as the Sessions Judge failed to properly appreciate the age of majority as defined in Majority Act (Act No. XVIII of 1975) read with Guardian and Wards Act (Act No. VIII of 1890) by which the age of the majority has been fixed at 18 years. Further, the Sessions Judge failed to consider the provision of law as provided in the Child Marriage Act, 1929 (Act XXIX of 1929) where the age of the female for marriage has been fixed at 18 years and upwards. 

 "Person marrying a minor below the age of 16 years may be guilty of offence under Child Marriage Act 1929 or of kidnapping under section 363 of the Penal Code. However under Muslim Law, puberty of girl is presumed at age of 15 and on attaining that age she can validly enter into contract of marriage. Girl of absolutely mature looks and talk, of her own volition contracting manage with a person and abandoning her parental protection and home to reside with her husband could not, when produced before the Court, be directed to be lodged in Darul Aman but should be allowed to go with her husband, if she so desires." 

 Section 19 of the Guardian and Wards Act 1890 provides as follows: 

 "Nothing in this Chapter shall authorise the Court to appoint or declare a guardian of the property of a minor whose property is under the superintendence of a Court of Wards, or to appoint or declare a guardian of the person. 

 a) of a minor who is a married female and whose husband is not, in the opinion of the Court, unfit to be guardian of her person, or 

 16. We have already quoted the order passed by the Sessions Judge dated 4.7.92 which is Annexure 'D' to the petition. The order clearly states that the petitioner Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy is permitted to remain present before the Medical Board for identification of the victim girl. We have also seen from the lower court's record that the victim girl while agreeing to be examined by the medical board attached her photograph to the agreement dated 23.6.92 and the father of the victim girl namely Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy had signed that agreement as an identifier. We have also seen that the medical report issued by the Radiologist of the medical examination carried out on 16.7.92, also bears the signature of the victim's father Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy. Therefore, the direction given by the Sessions Judge that the father of the victim girl be permitted to appear before the medical board for identification of the victim girl had been met. So far as the date of holding further medical examination is concerned the Principal of Chittagong Medical College had directed that the medical examination be completed 'within' 22.7.92 So, by holding the second medical examination on 2l.7.92 that is, within 22.7.92, there was no departure from, or violation of the order/direction of the Principal of Chittagong Medical College which said that the medical examination be completed 'within' 22.7.92. The purpose of allowing• the victim's father to be present before the medical board was clearly for a limited purpose to prove the victim's identity. This having been complied with both at the time the victim girl agreed to be examined by her Memo dated 23.6.92 and again when Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy put his signature on the medical report dated 16.7.92 as identifier, there appears to be no violation of the order of carrying out medical examination of victim Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua to determine her age. It also appears from the medical report of 16.7.92 issued by the Radiologist who was the chairman of the medical board that SI Md. Mominul Islam of Lohagara Police Station was also present and had identified the victim girl by signing the medical report. 

 18. We have already quoted the medical report signed on 18.7.92 by the Radiologist after the medical examination of victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua was held on 16.7.92. According to the report, victim Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua was between 15 and 16 years on 16.7.92. We have also quoted the medical report held on 16.7.92 and on 21.7.92 which was signed on 30.8.92 by all the 3 doctors constituting the Medical Board namely, Dr. Hashim Ahmed, Professor of Radiology, Chittagong Medical College, Dr. Anwar Ara Begum Associate Professor Forensic Medicine Department and Dr. Shamsun Nahar, Associate Professor, Department of Gynaecology. According to them, the age of victim Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua, daughter of Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy of village Padua, Police Station Lohagara, Chittagong was between 15 to 16 years on 21.7.92. It was on the basis of this medical report that the Sessions Judge prima facie came to the opinion that the victim girl was 16 years 6/7 months on 27.4.93 that is the date on which he delivered the impugned judgment. The victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua also appeared before this court on 17.8.92. Although it is not possible to correctly state her age, she appeared to us to be over 16 years and the prima facie calculation by the Sessions Judge Chittagong that the victim girl Ayesha Siddiqua's age was at least 16 years 6 months on 21.4.93 appears to be correct for the purpose of disposal of the petition. This is also our prima facie observation which will not prejudice the trial, and the trial Court is at liberty to decide the actual age of the victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua. 

 "Where a person brought before the Court is aged 16 years or over, the will of such person, when the question before the Court is whether she (or he) should be detained or allowed to go from Court's custody, must be allowed to prevail. The position of such a person is, at the most, that of a witness and therefore not being an accused she or he cannot be detained against her (or his) will." 

 "Question of custody loses its relevance when the girl concerned is found to be aged over 16 years. She neither being an accused or a witness in the case cannot be held in detention under court's order but is free to go to any place of her liking." 

 21. This view was also supported in the case of Manindra Kumar Malakar Vs. Secretary, Minstry of Home Affairs and others reported in 43 DLR 71. In the case of Fatema Begum alias Urmila Rani Vs. Ganeswar Nath and State reported in 1989 BLD 469 a Division Bench of this court held that a Magistrate cannot detain a person unless he or she is an accused in a criminal case and when above the age of 16 cannot be said to be a minor within the meaning of kidnapping under the Penal Code. It was held in that case the girl being over 16 years cannot be handed over to her father or to anybody but had to be set at liberty. 

 22. On the other hand, in the case of Sukhendra Chandra Das Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 42 DLR 79 a Division Bench of this Court (in which one of us was a party), reliance was placed primarily on the Majority Act of 1875 which has fixed the age of majority to be 18 years and the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 (as amended by Ordinance No. XXXVIII of 1984) making those contracting a marriage of a girl below the age of 18 years and a boy below the age of 21 years a punishable offence. It was observed that under the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 read with Majority Act, 1875 any person (male or female) below the age of 18 years was a minor for the purpose of guardianship of minor persons and property, and therefore held: 

 "For the purpose of custody of the girl age of majority laid down in the Majority Act, 1875 read with the Guardian and Wards Act, 1890 i.e. the age of 18 years is the determining factor to decide whether the girl is to be given to the custody of the guardian." 

 24. This view was also supported by another Division Bench of this court in the case of Sumati Begum Vs. Rafiqueullah and State reported in 44 DLR 500. Then in the case of Muthu Ibrahim Vs. Emperor reported in ILR 37 (Mad.) 567 that for the purpose of lawful guardianship the age of majority is that as laid down in section 3 of the Majority Act, 1875. Though a Mohammadan female attains majority upon her attaining puberty under Mohammadan law she is still minor and subject to the control of the guardian till she attains majority, that is, till she becomes sui juris according to Majority Act 1875. 

 26. We have already said that the victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua appeared before us in the presence of her father informant petitioner Dr. Bimal Kanti Roy, her mother and elder sister. The victim girl with nobody excepting her father and her mother in the chamber of the court declined to go with her father in spite of repeated persuasion by both the parents. She wanted to go with her husband, and she said-that if that was not allowed she preferred to remain in the judicial custody in the jail. She begged not to be sent to her parents. She also made a statement in court stating that her father's name was Bimal Kanti Roy and her mother's name Shefali Roy. Her parents had 4 sons and 5 daughters. She was the youngest of the 9 children. Her father had a medicine shop at Padua and also practiced there as a village doctor in the said village. Her 3 elder sisters were married. Her immediate elder sister Munmun Roy was older than her by 2/3 years. Her own age at present was 19 years. She read upto class IX at Padua High School. Accused Md. Saiful Islam Munni was son of Mr. Md. Islam Chowdhury who was Manager of Padua branch of Pubali Bank and has now been transferred to Agrabad branch of Pubali Bank, Chittagong. Accused Md. Saiful Islam passed his SSC Examination in Second Division. He was aged about 26 years and at the time of occurrence he used to do business in timber. Her two elder brothers Joy Prakash Roy and Rumu Roy had become Muslim and were now named Serajul Islam and Shamsul Islam respectively. She embraced Islam voluntarily and thereafter on 9.6.92 she got married to the accused of her own free will according to Muslim Law under a written registered Nikanama and the marriage was registered by the Muslim Nika registrar Kazi, Hathazari Union, District Chittagong on 9.6.92. Her brother Serajul Islam who was previously called Joy Prakash became her 'vaqil' and signed the Nikanama. She has further stated that if she was forcibly sent to the custody of her parents the Hindu society would never accept her as she had already embraced Islam and married a Muslim with whom she had lived for quite some time as husband and wife as the Magistrate of Lohagara had allowed her to live with her husband. She further apprehends that no Hindu gentleman of any worth would marry her. Her parents might get her married to some unworthy person by paying cash (Joutuk) of taka two lakh or so but after spending that amount that man would abandon her on the ground that she had embraced Islam and married a Muslim and would thus become a 'Kulata' (outcast). She also stated that accused Saiful Islam was her lover and used to meet her often and she became pregnant. Her pregnancy was terminated by abortion. She told this fact to the doctors who also found this to be true and noted the fact in their medical report 

 27. Apart from this statement of the girl we have seen from the lower court's record that she swore an affidavit before a First Class Magistrate Hathazari, Chittagong on 7.6.92 that she had voluntarily embraced Islam on Friday after Jumma prayers on 5.6.92 by reciting 'kalema' before the Imam of the Chand Mia Chowdhury Jame Masjid. There is also a photo copy of the registered Nikanama registering the marriage of Ayesha Siddiqua alias Munni Roy with accused Saiful Islam on 9.7.92. It appears from the registered Nikanama that she was given in marriage to accused Saiful Islam by her brother Serajul Islam previously known as Joy Prakash Roy by putting his signature. The Nikanama was also signed by other witnesses. Mr. Muqbul Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the girl, had argued that because the marriage was valid, the husband had become the guardian of the girl and that therefore it was correctly held that she was free to go any where she liked. We may observe here that the question whether the girl could have embraced Islam before she became sui juries and the question of validity of this marriage are to decided in the appropriate court. 

 28. With regard to maintainability of this application under section 561A CrPC it has been held in Shahabul Huda Vs. Md. Shaft reported in BCR 1984 (AD) 468 that an application under section 561A for quashing the proceedings under section 145 CrPC shall not amount to second revision barred under section 439(4) CrPC simply bcause the petitioner unsuccessfully moved the Sessions Judge before filing the application before the High Court under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The Appellate Division held that no criminal court could oust from posession an existing occupier of a premises by way of drawing up of proceeding and attaching the premises. In their opinion, drawing up of proceeding was clearly an abuse of the process of the court and in order to prevent the abuse of the process of the court and to secure justice they should interfere with the order. Then in the case of Fatema Begum alias Urmila Rani Vs. Gageswar Nath and State reported in 1989 BLD 469 a Division Bench of this court held that the Sessions Judge in an application under section 439 CrPC had misapplied the provision of the Child Marriage Restraint Act, Bangladesh Majority Act and thereby acted illegally in affirming the unauthorised order passed by the learned Magistrate, Therefore it was necessary to interfere under section 561A CrPC to prevent abuse of the process of the court and tp secure ends of justice. In the instant case also we find that the order of the Sessions Judge, Chittagong was illegal under the circumstances and it is necessary of to interfere to secure the ends to justice. 

 29. In view of the circumstances which we have narrated above, we are of the view that the victim girl Munni Roy alias Ayesha Siddiqua should be free from all external influences during the trial. In the event she is called upon to depose, she should be able to give her evidence freely without any interference, coercion or influence, So far as her age is concerned, the prima facie finding is that she was at least 16 years 6 months on 27.4.93. We have also seen her and it appears to us also that she would be of that age. If she was 16 years 6 months on 27.4.93, her approximate date of birth prima facie would be around 27.10.76. Although she has not been cited as a witness in the charge sheet, it is apparent that she is a vital witness who may be called upon to depose either by the Court or by any other party. Besides, we also find that charge sheet has been submitted against the accused persons under section 366A of the Penal Code which is an offence for procuring a girl under the age of 18 years by inducement with the intent that the girl may be seduced to illicil intercourse with 'another person'. The minor to be taken out of the lawful custody of the lawful guardians as under section 363 must be a minor under 16 years of age. Therefore minor under the age of 18 years would be referable only to section 366A which is applicable in the isnstant case according to the charge sheet submitted by prosecution. We have also seen that the age of majority for a girl is 18 years under the Majority Act. So she cannot be allowed to go wherever she wants until she attains the age of 18 years. In the case of Dr. Kazi Mozammel Hoque Vs. State reported in 45 DLR 197 a Division Bench of this Court has held that the judicial custody of a victim girl is different from detention of a criminal or political detenu. Judicial custody of a victim girl has the complexion of the custody of a guardian. This custody is necessary for giving the girl a chance to be free from external influence. Section 100 of the CrPC authorised the Metropolitan Magistrate, Magistrate 1st Class, etc to issue search warrants for recovery of persons wrongly confined and if found make such order as in the circumstances of the case seems proper. 

 The trial Court is directed to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within six months. Let the lower Court records be sent down at once with a copy of this Judgment.
